extracted.intended_audience: applicants, utilities, cable operators, telecommunications carriers, agencies, and other parties participating in FCC environmental reviews and pole-attachment complaint proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural standards in 47 CFR Part 1 covering preparation and use of Environmental Impact Statements (EIS), section 106 historic-preservation review, and pole-attachment complaint procedures (access, complaints, evidence, rates, remedies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Intent contents for EISs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice shall briefly identify the proposal, concisely describe the environmental issues and concerns presented by the subject application, and generally invite participation from affected or involved agencies, authorities and other interested persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish in the Federal Register a Notice of Intent to prepare EISs; the Notice should identify proposal, describe environmental issues/concerns, and invite participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS scope excludes non-environmental considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The EISs shall not address non-environmental considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid repetition and length, Statements should, where feasible, incorporate by reference material in previous documents with only a brief summary; Bureau will identify and address significant environmental issues and eliminate insignificant issues from analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bureau authority to request additional information and studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau may request further information from the applicant, interested persons and agencies and authorities; may direct that technical studies be made by the applicant and obtain expert opinion concerning potential environmental problems and costs, and comparative analyses of alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureau may consult experts to identify mitigation measures and alternatives; may direct that objections be raised with appropriate land use agencies if views not previously sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementation of EISs when new information arises
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau responsible for processing the application shall draft supplements to Statements where significant new circumstances occur or information arises relevant to environmental concerns and bearing upon the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementation duty attaches to the Bureau preparing the EIS for the particular application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative record composition and electronic filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Application, the EA, the DEIS, and the FEIS and all related documents, including the comments filed by the public and any agency, shall be part of the administrative record and will be routinely available for public inspection. All documents and comments shall be filed electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative record must include the listed documents and comments; filing is electronic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant notice to community of availability and hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: If EISs are to be prepared, the applicant must provide the community with notice of the availability of environmental documents and the scheduling of any Commission hearings in that action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant responsibility to notify community about availability and hearing schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing restrictions after Notice of Availability
rubrics_metrics.description: No decision shall be made until ninety (90) days after the Notice of Availability of the Draft Environmental Impact Statement is published in the Federal Register, and thirty (30) days after the Notice of Availability of the Final Environmental Impact Statement is published in the Federal Register, which time period may run concurrently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing of agency action governed by 40 CFR 1506.10; see referenced CFR provisions and FCC sections for concurrency rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEIS required content — description of proposal and affected area
rubrics_metrics.description: The DEIS shall include a concise description of the proposal, the nature of the area affected, its uses, and any specific feature of the area that has special environmental significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DEIS must concisely describe proposal and environmental context including specially significant features.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEIS required content — analysis and reasonable alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The DEIS shall include an analysis of the proposal, and reasonable alternatives exploring the important consequent advantages and/or disadvantages of the action and indicating the direct and indirect effects and their significance in terms of the short and long-term uses of the human environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis must cover alternatives, advantages/disadvantages, direct/indirect effects and their significance over short and long term.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEIS distribution and notice procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When a DEIS and supplements are prepared, the Commission shall file the Statement with the Office of Federal Activities, EPA; Public Notice of the availability of the DEIS will be published in the Federal Register by EPA. Copies or summaries will be electronically mailed with a request for comment to federal agencies with jurisdiction or expertise, the Council on Environmental Quality, the applicant, and interested individuals and agencies; hard copies provided by mail if requested by those lacking electronic access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure mailing and publication procedures follow EPA and Commission practices; provide hardcopies on request if requester lacks email access.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEIS public comment period and filing format
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person or agency may comment on the DEIS and the environmental effect of the proposal within 45 days after notice of availability is published in the Federal Register. A copy of those comments shall be electronically mailed to the applicant by the person who files them pursuant to § 1.47 and filed electronically with the Commission. If unable or unreasonably burdensome to file electronically, comments may be submitted by mail with a request for waiver under § 1.1304(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be filed electronically and emailed to applicant; waiver process exists for burdensome cases; 45-day comment window applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenter qualifications and agency comment identification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person submitting comments is especially qualified in any way to comment on the environmental impact of the facilities, a statement of his or her qualifications shall be set out in the comments. Comments submitted by an agency shall identify the person(s) who prepared them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include qualifications when relevant; agency comments must identify preparers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant reply comments timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may electronically file reply comments within 15 days after the time for filing comments has expired. Reply comments shall be filed with the Commission and served by the applicant on persons or agencies which filed comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must serve reply comments to commenting parties; 15-day reply period.

rubrics_metrics.name: FEIS required content — summary, responses, analysis, alternatives, recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The FEIS shall include a summary of the comments, and a response to the comments, and an analysis of the proposal in terms of its environmental consequences, and any reasonable alternatives, and recommendations, if any, and shall cite the Commission's internal appeal procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FEIS must attach comments or summaries where voluminous; distribute/publish as DEIS per § 1.1315.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of FEIS in hearing and non-hearing matters
rubrics_metrics.description: In rendering an initial decision, the presiding officer shall use the FEIS in considering the environmental issues, together with all other non-environmental issues. When the Commission serves as presiding officer or upon its review, the Commission will consider and assess all aspects of the FEIS and will render its decision, giving due consideration to the environmental and nonenvironmental issues. In all non-hearing matters, the Commission will review the FEIS along with other relevant issues to ensure environmental effects are specifically assessed and given comprehensive consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FEIS must be integrated into the decision-making record and receive explicit consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106 historic properties review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Commission undertaking that has the potential to cause effects on historic properties, unless excluded, shall be subject to review under section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act by applying the procedures in 36 CFR 800.3-800.13, or, if applicable, a program alternative established pursuant to 36 CFR 800.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program alternatives include specified Nationwide Programmatic Agreements and program comments listed in Appendix B/C; follow the cited 36 CFR procedures or approved program alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories excluded from Section 106 review
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusions include: (1) projects reviewed by other agencies where another agency is lead federal agency; (2) projects subject to program alternatives established under 36 CFR 800.14; (3) replacement utility poles meeting specific criteria; (4) collocations on buildings and other non-tower structures meeting listed conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each exclusion has detailed subcriteria (see replacement pole and collocation criteria) that must be satisfied to qualify for exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement pole exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A replacement for an existing structure is excluded where all criteria are satisfied: original structure is a pole capable of holding utility/communications lines, was not originally erected primarily to support antennas, and is not itself a historic property; replacement pole is located no more than 10 feet away (and no new ground disturbance), height not exceed original by more than 5 feet or 10% (whichever greater), and appearance consistent with original pole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground disturbance defined; distance measured between centerpoints; no new ground disturbance includes not exceeding previously disturbed areas including temporary supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collocation exclusion conditions on buildings/non-tower structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Mounting antennas on buildings or non-tower structures is excluded if the deployment meets conditions: there is an existing antenna; one of Non-Visible Antennas, Visible Replacement Antennas, or Other Visible Antennas criteria is met (each with subcriteria regarding visibility, replacement, size limits, cabinet visibility); deployment complies with zoning and historic preservation conditions that mitigate effects; involves no new ground disturbance; and would not otherwise require preparation of an EA solely because of structure age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note defines 'same vicinity' and 'no new ground disturbance' and lists numeric size/visibility limits (e.g., not more than 3 feet larger) and location-distance rules (within ten feet centerpoint).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibilities for Section 106 and program alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants seeking Commission authorization for construction or modification of towers, collocation of antennas, or other undertakings shall take the steps mandated by, and comply with the requirements set forth in, Appendix C of this part, sections III–X, or any other applicable program alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow Appendix C or applicable program alternative procedural steps for Section 106 review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for environmental and pole-attachment context
rubrics_metrics.description: Key defined terms include: Antenna; Applicant; Collocation; Tower; Undertaking; Utility; Pole attachment; Usable space; Complaint; Complainant; Defendant; State; Telecommunications carrier; Conduit; Conduit system; Duct; Unusable space; Attaching entity; Inner-duct; Make-ready; Complex make-ready; Simple make-ready; Communications space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions specify scope and limits of terms used throughout the Part; they determine applicability of duties, exclusions, and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to provide nondiscriminatory access to poles, ducts, conduits, rights-of-way
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility shall provide a cable television system or any telecommunications carrier with nondiscriminatory access to any pole, duct, conduit, or right-of-way owned or controlled by it. A utility may deny access on a non-discriminatory basis where there is insufficient capacity or for reasons of safety, reliability and generally applicable engineering purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denials must be on nondiscriminatory bases and may be for capacity, safety, reliability, or engineering reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written requests and written denials with supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for access must be in writing. If access is not granted within specified time periods, the utility must confirm the denial in writing by the applicable deadline. The utility's denial shall be specific, include all relevant evidence and information supporting its denial, and explain how such evidence relates to denial for lack of capacity, safety, reliability or engineering standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely written confirmation and factual explanation are required when denying access.

rubrics_metrics.name: 60-day notice requirement for removal, rate increases, or facility modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility shall provide a cable operator or telecommunications carrier no less than 60 days written notice prior to: (1) Removal of facilities or termination of any service to those facilities arising out of a rate, term or condition of the attachment agreement; (2) Any increase in pole attachment rates; or (3) Any modification of facilities by the utility other than make-ready noticed pursuant to § 1.1411(f), routine maintenance, or modification in response to emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 60-day written notice requirement ensures advance notice except for listed exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for Temporary Stay requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A cable operator or telecommunications carrier may file a 'Petition for Temporary Stay' within 15 days of receipt of a 60-day notice. The petition must include in concise terms the relief sought, the reasons for such relief including a showing of irreparable harm and likely cessation of service, a copy of the notice, and certification of service as required by § 1.1404(b). The named may file an answer within 7 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further filings will be considered unless requested or authorized by the Commission; no extensions of time except per § 1.46.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint filing formalities and required attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Pole attachment complaints are governed by subpart E formal complaint rules, must be accompanied by a certification of service on the named defendant and relevant governmental agencies. Where claiming a rate/term/condition unjust, complaint shall state that the State has not certified regulation to the Commission and include a copy of any pole attachment agreement or statements that the utility uses/controls poles and that complainant currently has attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainant must include factual foundations and service certification; lack of agreement requires specific statements of usage and attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity and evidentiary data required in complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The complaint shall state with specificity the pole attachment rate, term or condition which is claimed to be unjust or unreasonable and provide all data and information supporting such claim. Data and information (including all necessary for applying rate formulas in § 1.1406) should be based upon historical or original cost methodology insofar as possible and derived from ARMIS, FERC Form 1, or other reports filed with state or federal regulatory agencies (identify source). The complainant shall also specify any other information and argument relied upon to attempt to establish that a rate, term, or condition is not just and reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authoritative regulatory filings and cost methodologies where possible; identify sources for data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility obligation to provide supporting information within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility must supply a cable operator or telecommunications carrier the information required in paragraph (e) along with supporting pages from ARMIS, FERC Form 1, or other reports and calculations within 30 days of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utilities have a strict 30-day provision obligation for requested cost/supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints not dismissed for utility failure to provide information
rubrics_metrics.description: If the information required is not provided to the complainant upon reasonable request, the complainant shall include a statement indicating steps taken to obtain the information, including dates. No complaint shall be dismissed where the utility has failed to provide the information after such reasonable request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainant must document efforts to obtain information; lack of utility cooperation will not cause dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for lack of jurisdiction when state certification exists
rubrics_metrics.description: The complaint shall be dismissed for lack of jurisdiction where a suitable certificate has been filed by a State that it regulates rates, terms and conditions for pole attachments, or where defendant or State offers proof the State regulates such access, or if utility does not use or control poles or does not meet § 1.1402(a) criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State certification must meet specified elements and is conclusive proof of lack of Commission jurisdiction; Commission will publish notice and compile listings of certifying states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptive absence of state regulation unless certification shows otherwise
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be rebuttably presumed that the state is not regulating pole attachments if the Commission does not receive certification from a state that: (1) It regulates rates, terms and conditions; (2) It considers consumer interests of both attachment services and utility services; and (3) It has issued and made effective rules implementing the state's regulatory authority including a specific methodology made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must be by order of the state regulatory body or by delegated authority with citation of law/regulation conferring such authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission's burden and parties' burdens in complaint proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The complainant has the burden of establishing a prima facie case that the rate, term, or condition is not just and reasonable or that denial of access violates 47 U.S.C. 224(f). If a utility argues a proposed rate is lower than its incremental costs, the utility has the burden of establishing that such rate is below the statutory minimum; in a denial of access case, the utility has the burden of proving the denial was lawful once a prima facie case is established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden-shifting rules apply depending on the issues raised (rate vs denial of access).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'just and reasonable' rate
rubrics_metrics.description: A rate is just and reasonable if it assures a utility the recovery of not less than the additional costs of providing pole attachments, nor more than an amount determined by multiplying the percentage of the total usable space (or duct/conduit capacity) occupied by the pole attachment by the sum of the operating expenses and actual capital costs of the utility attributable to the entire pole, duct, conduit, or right-of-way. The Commission shall exclude from actual capital costs those reimbursements received by the utility from cable operators and telecommunications carriers for non-recurring costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the percentage-of-space allocator against operating expenses plus actual capital costs (with stated exclusions) to determine upper bound; ensure cost bases follow specified accounting methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulas for determining maximum just and reasonable rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will apply specified formulas for attachments to poles and conduits. For poles, Rate = Space Factor × Cost with Cost expressed as Net Cost of a Bare Pole × Carrying Charge Rate multiplied by a factor that depends on the number of Attaching Entities (e.g., 0.66 for 5 attaching entities; 0.56 for 4; etc.); alternative and conduit formulas also apply and the higher applicable rate is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the tabulated space-factor multipliers based on number of attaching entities; interpolate for non-integer numbers; conduit and inner-duct fractions rules apply (if no inner-duct installed fraction presumed 1/2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting options and Implementation Rate Difference for opt-out carriers
rubrics_metrics.description: A price cap company, or rate-of-return carrier electing to provide service pursuant to § 61.50, that opts-out of part 32 may calculate attachment rates using either part 32 accounting data or GAAP accounting data. A company using GAAP accounting data to compute rates in any of the first twelve years after opting-out must adjust its annually computed GAAP-based rates by an Implementation Rate Difference for each of the remaining years in the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation Rate Difference equals the difference between attachment rates calculated under part 32 and under GAAP as of the last full year preceding the carrier's initial opting-out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies available when rates/terms/conditions are unjust or access unlawfully denied
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission determines the rate, term, or condition is not just and reasonable, it may prescribe a just and reasonable rate, terminate the unjust/unreasonable rate/term/condition, substitute the established ones in the agreement, and/or order a refund or payment (normally the difference plus interest). If access has been unlawfully denied or delayed, it may order that access be permitted within a specified time frame and in accordance with specified rates, terms, and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refunds/payments include difference between amounts paid and commission-established amounts plus interest consistent with statutes of limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputation of pole-attachment rates for utilities providing telecom/cable services
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility that engages in provision of telecommunications or cable services shall impute to its costs of providing such services (and charge any affiliate engaged in such services) an equal amount to the pole attachment rate for which such company would be liable under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imputation ensures affiliates bear pole-attachment costs analogous to outside attaching entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of modification (make-ready) costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The costs of modifying a facility shall be borne by all parties that obtain access to the facility as a result of the modification and by all parties that directly benefit from the modification; each party shall share proportionately. A party with a preexisting attachment is deemed to directly benefit if, after notification of modification, it adds to or modifies its attachment. Preexisting parties shall not be required to bear costs of rearranging/replacing their attachment if necessitated solely by another party's additional attachment; parties attaching after completion of modification share proportionately if modification rendered the added attachment possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish complex make-ready (may cause outages) from simple make-ready; cost-sharing principles apply proportionately to beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of unusable space costs
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility shall apportion the cost of providing unusable space on a pole so that such apportionment equals two-thirds of the costs of providing unusable space that would be allocated to such entity under an equal apportionment among all attaching entities. All attaching entities attached to the pole shall be counted for apportioning the cost of unusable space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utilities may use rebuttable presumptive averages when calculating number of attaching entities: non-urbanized service areas (under 50,000 population) presumptive average = 3; urbanized (50,000 or higher) presumptive average = 5.
